bandReport.notes: Q41-Q57, contiguous, no gaps. SEAMS BOTH CLEAN, checked against the neighbouring pages I do not own: p03 ends with Q40 complete (all four options printed on p03), so Q41 opens my band cleanly; p07 opens with Q58 complete, so Q57 ends it cleanly. NO Directions / 'for the next N items' block anywhere in p03-p07 — I read the page before mine and the page after mine specifically to check, and there is none, so no question in this band carries context/setLabel. Q41-Q44 LOOK like a set but are not: each is a self-contained 'Consider a question and two statements' item with its own Question and its own two statements, so they carry no shared stimulus. NOTE the option wording differs between them and must not be normalised — Q41 and Q42 print 'is sufficient to answer the question' while Q43 and Q44 print 'is required to answer the question', and their (d) options differ correspondingly ('Both ... are not sufficient' vs 'Neither ... nor ... is required'). NO FIGURES in this band: Q53 and Q54 are heights-and-distances items but both are stated entirely in words with no diagram printed, and no other item references one. The booklet's raised middle dot appears in this band as a DECIMAL separator once (Q41 Statement-I, printed '-29·8', transcribed -29.8, glyph confirmed at 7x) and as a MULTIPLICATION dot twice in Q55 ('tan a · tan b', 'sec^2 a · sec^2 b', written \cdot) — the two uses are on different pages and were distinguished by reading each at 7x, not by rule. cosec is written \operatorname{cosec}, matching the convention already used in the 2020-1 and 2023-1 band files. Verified: check-bands.ts reports this band 0 errors / 0 warnings, and all 94 of its math zones render through the repo's own KaTeX with 0 failures (both probes were also driven with deliberately broken copies first, and both went red, so the green is real).

questions.stem:
Consider a question and two statements :

Question :

Is \(3x + 2y\) positive?

Statement-I : \(x^3 = -29.8\)

Statement-II : \(y^3 = 3x\)

Which one of the following is correct in respect of the question and the statements?

options.label: A
options.text: Statement-I alone is sufficient to answer the question

options.label: B
options.text: Statement-II alone is sufficient to answer the question

options.label: C
options.text: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are together sufficient to answer the question

options.label: D
options.text: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are not sufficient to answer the question

questions.stem:
If \(A\), \(B\), \(C\) are acute angles and

\(\sin(B + C - A) = \cos(C + A - B) = \tan(A + B - C) = 1\)

then what is \((A + B + C)\) equal to?

If \(A\), \(B\), \(C\), \(D\) are the angles of a cyclic quadrilateral, then what is the value of the following?

\(\sin\left(\frac{A + C}{2}\right) + \sin\left(\frac{B + D}{2}\right)\)

An aeroplane is observed to be approaching the airport. It is at a distance of 10 km from the point of observation on the ground and makes an angle of elevation \(\theta\). If the aeroplane is at a height of 8 km above the ground, then which one of the following is correct?

The angle of elevation of the top of a tower of height \(x\) metre from a point on the ground is found to be \(60^\circ\). By going \(y\) metre away from that point, it becomes \(30^\circ\). Which one of the following relations is correct?
If \(\tan\theta + \sec\theta = 3\), then what is the value of \(3\tan\theta + 9\sec\theta\)?

Consider the following :

1. \(\sqrt{\sec^2\theta + \operatorname{cosec}^2\theta} = \tan\theta + \cot\theta\), where \(0 < \theta < 90^\circ\)

2. \(\sqrt{\tan^2\theta + \cot^2\theta + 4} = \sec\theta + \operatorname{cosec}\theta\), where \(0 < \theta < 90^\circ\)

Which of the above is/are an identity/identities?
